pages.text: "Me first! I'll drink first!" Tumba stamped on the red dirt path. Today they would race Kiki to the water. Tumba was already huffing through their nose.
"Go!" Off they ran—but Tumba tripped on a stone. Kiki reached the water first. Tumba's face flushed. "Squeee! Again! Do it again!" they yelled.
Tumba dug furiously with their snout. A cloud of dust rose. Coughing, Kiki hid behind a rock. "Tumba's angry again..." In the dust, Tumba's eyes grew wet.
Mom approached slowly. "Something hot rushed up inside you, didn't it?" Tumba sniffled and nodded. "That's anger. Anger isn't bad. Like this dust, it comes and goes."
"What do I do?" Tumba asked. Mom smiled. "Stop digging. Breathe in through your nose—tummy out! Breathe out slowly through your snout. Then the dust can settle." She tapped Tumba's tummy.
"Together. One, breathe in. Two, breathe out..." Tumba followed, tummy rounding. The dust settled and Kiki's face appeared behind the rock. Mom sang, "Feeling angry? Breathe out!"
With a softer heart, Tumba bravely approached Kiki. "Sorry I shouted. I got angry all at once. Now I've breathed out." Their tail popped up. Feeling angry? Breathe out!
"It's okay, Tumba!" Kiki hopped onto the rock and waved a paw. Laughter returned to the quiet shore.
They raced again, and Tumba lost again. Anger stirred, but Tumba stopped, breathed in, then out. "One, stop digging! Two, breathe in! Three, breathe out! I can try again next time!"

Mom curled her neck around Tumba. "Knowing how to let anger go makes you a real winner!" A slow breath helped anger settle like dust. Feeling angry? Breathe out! The friends laughed and played by the water.
